publications.name: Social Gym and SPaRTan: Benchmarking and Improving LLM Social Reasoning via Multi-Agent Game Tournaments
publications.author: Keyu He, Xuhui Zhou, Maarten Sap
publications.summary: Social Gym is a benchmark of 21 multi-agent social games with verifiable, objective outcomes; SPaRTan is a training-free self-play and reflect-transfer loop that produces transferable playbooks improving LLM social reasoning across games and models.

publications.name: RECAP: An End-to-End Platform for Capturing, Replaying, and Analyzing AI-Assisted Programming Interactions
publications.author: Keyu He*, Qianou Ma*, Valerie Chen, Wayne Chi, Tongshuang Wu
publications.summary: RECAP captures AI chat and code edits in VS Code, merges them into replayable timelines, and provides analysis modules for studying developer-AI interaction patterns.

publications.name: Believing without Seeing: Quality Scores for Contextualizing Vision-Language Model Explanations
publications.author: Keyu He, Tejas Srinivasan, Brihi Joshi, Xiang Ren, Jesse Thomason, Swabha Swayamdipta
publications.summary: We introduce Visual Fidelity and Contrastiveness -- two explanation quality scores that help users more appropriately rely on vision-language model predictions without seeing the image.

publications.name: ELI-Why: Evaluating the Pedagogical Utility of LLM Explanations
publications.author: Brihi Joshi*, Keyu He*, Sahana Ramnath, Sadra Sabouri, Kaitlyn Zhou, Souti Chattopadhyay, Swabha Swayamdipta, Xiang Ren
publications.summary: Evaluate the pedagogical utility of LLMs in tailoring explanations to users with different educational backgrounds.

publications.name: Attributing Culture-Conditioned Generations to Pretraining Corpora
publications.author: Huihan Li*, Arnav Goel*, Keyu He, Xiang Ren
publications.summary: This paper introduces MEMOed, a framework to analyze whether AI generations are driven by memorization or generalization, with a focus on cultural symbols.

publications.name: Enhancing Debugging Skills of LLMs with Prompt Engineering
publications.author: Keyu He*, Max Li*, and Joseph Liu*
publications.summary: Study on improving LLM debugging through prompt engineering techniques. Evaluated few-shot learning and chain-of-thought approaches on GPT-3.5, revealing limitations in current debugging capabilities.

work.name: Adobe
highlights: Shipped 5+ agent skills, including a four-skill family outside the team's own domain, through an agent skill generator merged into the team's shared skill repo, which turns rough developer requests into standards-compliant skills, grounding against internal prior art so existing work isn't rebuilt and self-auditing against the agentskills.io spec.

Developed the systematic quality measure for the team's agent recommendation pipeline, a reference-free 6-dimension rubric combining LLM-as-judge with deterministic checks, reproducible to 0.01–0.05 per-dimension variance across repeated runs and surfacing two systematic weaknesses for the team to act on.

Took that measure to production across the org, porting it onto the internal GenAI evaluation service as a reusable scorer and staging it end-to-end for two enterprise customers, on a four-stage Databricks pipeline built to run it.

work.name: CMind
highlights: Built a LangChain-based RAG prototype over an internal analytics DB (chunking, embeddings, FAISS indexing/retrieval, LLM answer synthesis) with metadata filters and notebook/API utilities.
Designed CEO-speech trait metrics and an auto-evaluation pipeline with custom rubrics, achieving Fleiss' κ of 0.89–0.91 against human annotations.

projects.name: VLM Hallucination Mitigation
projects.summary: Training-free latent reflection for vision-language models, at Carnegie Mellon University.
highlights: Built a training-free latent reflection module that monitors decoding entropy and injects reflection steps when the model is uncertain.
Benchmarked against DAMO, VCD, OPERA, and DeGF on POPE/RePOPE/MMBench across LLaVA-1.5-7B, InstructBLIP-7B, and Qwen2-VL-7B.
On RePOPE, raised LLaVA-1.5-7B accuracy from 84.0% to 90.3% with the lowest calibration error (ECE 0.028) among all methods compared.

projects.name: LLM Prompt Recovery
projects.summary: Developed a system to recover user prompts using fine-tuned Mixtral models, achieving top 3.4% in a Kaggle competition.
highlights: Achieved a score of 0.65 using sentence-T5-base and sharpened cosine similarity.
Ranked 75/2175 globally in the Kaggle competition.
Published fine-tuned model on Kaggle for broader access.

projects.name: AI-Based Career Advisor
projects.summary: Built an AI tool to assist users in planning career paths based on skills and interests.
highlights: Developed a Streamlit-based interactive UI integrating GPT-4o for job suggestions.
Implemented cosine similarity search for skill-job matching.
Integrated Bing AI for real-time job application link retrieval.

projects.name: Enhancing Debugging Skills of LLMs with Prompt Engineering
projects.summary: Improved LLM debugging capabilities through advanced prompt engineering techniques.
highlights: Experimented with various prompting strategies to enhance debugging efficiency.
Achieved significant improvements in LLM performance on debugging tasks.

projects.name: Automated Hate Speech Detection in Social Media
projects.summary: Developed an advanced ML model for detecting hate speech, achieving 94% accuracy.
highlights: Enhanced online safety and inclusivity through robust model optimization.
